vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — holds the July 9 evening level for the third consecutive session. The July 10 morning session's defining analytical signature is the market-geopolitical dislocation: Thursday's equity close of Dow +0.3%, S&P +0.8%, Nasdaq +1.3% occurred while US and Iranian forces were conducting their third consecutive day of military exchanges in and around the Strait of Hormuz. That market verdict — anchored by the SK Hynix $26.51B IPO (largest-ever foreign company Nasdaq debut) and broad AI/semiconductor strength — is the primary positive holding the session at Vibe 4. The market is pricing the Witkoff/Kushner negotiating channel as a credible institutional constraint on full-scale war resumption, consistent with the pattern of every prior escalation-and-pullback episode in the 133-day Hormuz arc. The primary negative anchor: Trump's 'ceasefire over' declaration from NATO Ankara (July 8) has not been formally retracted entering Friday morning. Oil sanctions on Iranian crude were reimposed July 7 — stripping the MOU's central economic incentive for Iranian participation. Tanker flow at ~25 vessels/day represents approximately 23% of the pre-war 110/day norm. WTI at ~$75 is a war-risk premium price, not a normalization-confidence price. CENTCOM executed the largest single-night strike package of the post-MOU arc on July 8 (approximately 90 targets across six Iranian provinces). Against these: no formal MOU termination instrument has been issued; no SNSC formal MOU-void declaration; no naval blockade reinstatement order; Kharg Island threatened but not struck; Iran has not issued a new formal MOU-void declaration under the July 8 oil-sanctions trigger; and Witkoff and Kushner publicly confirmed desire to continue negotiations with Trump acknowledging their channel. The Russia fuel crisis compounding at Day 10 (Omsk refinery halted; 78+ regions; ~25% offline) creates a secondary energy supply shock that reinforces Warsh's hawkish SEP bias at the Federal Reserve — the FOMC's June meeting pre-dated this crisis, so the September SEP will be the first formal assessment with full Russia-crisis data. Domestic infrastructure risk: Longview CSB T-1 to the July 11 three-thread convergence window is the morning's highest-specificity short-fuse risk. Chelan Hills Fire Day 6 faces the first Red Flag condition test of its containment arc. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: Witkoff/Kushner announce formal Iran communication channel with negotiation session scheduled; overnight July 10 exchange halt; WTI pullback from ~$75 toward $70-72 de-escalation range; Chelan Hills holds or advances containment through Red Flag Warning conditions. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: Iran SNSC formally voids MOU in response to oil-sanction reimposition; CENTCOM reinstates Project Freedom naval blockade or executes Kharg Island interdiction; Chelan Hills regression below 50% containment under Red Flag event; Longview CSB July 11 convergence materializes as confirmed safety incident.

items.summary: The July 10 morning brief opens on Hormuz Day 133 with the MOU under maximum declaratory stress for the third consecutive day and no decisive breach instrument in force as of 0700 Pacific time. The operative state of play entering Friday: Trump's 'as far as I'm concerned, it's over' declaration from the NATO summit close-out press conference in Ankara (July 8) has not been formally retracted. No US executive order or CENTCOM directive reinstating the Project Freedom naval blockade has been issued. No SNSC formal MOU-void declaration has been confirmed — Iran continues to operate under the June 26 IRGC cargo-strike re-closure rationale rather than a new formal MOU termination triggered by the July 7 oil-sanctions reimposition. CENTCOM executed what appears to be the largest single-night strike package of the post-MOU arc on the night of July 8, hitting approximately 90 targets across at least six Iranian provinces: Sirik, Qeshm, Bandar Abbas (Hormozgan), Iranshahr (Sistan-Baluchestan), Bushehr, Konarak, Chabahar, and Aq Qala (Golestan). Iran responded with strikes on 85 or more US military facilities across Bahrain and Kuwait — the largest single Iranian counter-strike package of the post-MOU period. One confirmed casualty was reported: a fireman killed at Iranshahr airport during the CENTCOM strikes. Overnight July 9-10, fresh exchanges were confirmed, extending the military contact into a third consecutive session. The critical analytical restraint on the Vibe downgrade entering Friday morning is the Kharg Island non-strike. Trump explicitly threatened to 'take over Kharg Island' — through which approximately 90% of Iranian oil exports transit — but CENTCOM has not confirmed any Kharg operation through the morning brief cycle. The non-strike on Kharg is the decisive negative-space indicator distinguishing a managed-pressure episode from an oil-export elimination campaign. The market's Thursday close (S&P +0.8%, Dow +0.3%, Nasdaq +1.3%) is itself the most functionally important geopolitical data point of the July 9 session: the equity market, having priced the May 19 'attack called off at Gulf allies' request' episode, the June 2 comms suspension resolution, and a dozen prior escalation-and-pullback sequences in this arc, is not pricing the MOU as having permanently collapsed. The Witkoff/Kushner negotiating channel — confirmed by both principals as wanting to continue, with Trump's own qualifier 'but they have to come back to me' preserving the off-ramp — is what the market is pricing as the operative constraint. The sixty-day nuclear compliance window (begun June 19; approximately August 17 endpoint) is 22 days elapsed at the start of July 10. Zero formal nuclear framework sessions have been held. The IAEA bombed-site inspection protocol has not been agreed. The oil sanctions reimposition on July 7 — revoking the Iranian crude export waiver that was the MOU's central economic incentive — is the most consequential formal US action of the post-MOU arc, more significant in structural terms than the declaratory 'over' language because it removes the commercial rationale for Iranian compliance. The waiver revocation creates a material incentive for Iran to escalate the intensity of its Hormuz interference, which is the primary escalation risk entering the weekend.

items.summary: Six secondary geopolitical threads entering July 10 morning. First: Russia fuel crisis Day 10. Omsk refinery — Russia's largest refinery and primary domestic gasoline producer, processing approximately 20 million metric tons of crude annually — halted operations on July 7 after Ukrainian drone strikes on July 6. Combined with prior Ukrainian infrastructure strikes, approximately one-quarter to one-third of Russia's total national refining capacity is now offline. Daily gasoline shortfall at approximately 20% below domestic demand. Fuel sales rationed to 20-30 liters per vehicle in affected regions. IEA has designated the crisis 'unprecedented' in scale for Russia's modern fuel infrastructure. 78 of 83 internationally recognized Russian regions reporting fuel access disruptions. The Russia fuel crisis creates a secondary energy supply disruption running concurrently with the Hormuz arc — a two-source global energy supply shock the June 17 FOMC minutes (which predated both the Russia crisis onset and the Hormuz MOU acute stress phase) did not assess. Chair Warsh's September SEP will be the first formal Fed assessment incorporating both supply disruptions. Second: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif traveled to Balochistan province Thursday to condole with families of 42 people — mostly security personnel — killed in multiple insurgent attacks this week. Sharif pledged to 'continue operations against militants' in the province. The multi-incident nature of the attacks (not a single event) suggests a coordinated insurgency escalation rather than an isolated incident. Balochistan is the site of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, and insurgency surges in the province carry infrastructure disruption implications for CPEC operations. Third: Lebanon fragile hold Day 25. The US-Iran-Lebanon ceasefire oversight committee (formed June 30) is nominally active. Hezbollah's 'null and void' declaration on the Rubio framework remains unretracted. IDF strike tempo reduced but not zero. The July 8-9 CENTCOM-Iran exchange adds uncertainty: if Iran characterizes the exchanges as license to direct Hezbollah to resume operations, the 'null and void' declaration becomes operational. No confirmed Iranian direction to Hezbollah as of July 10 morning. Fourth: Peru JNE credentials ceremony for Keiko Fujimori is T-5 days (July 15). Inauguration July 28 (T-18). Andean resource nationalism premium eliminated at JNE certification holds. Fifth: Colombia de la Espriella transition Day 8 (T-28 to August 7 inauguration). De la Espriella pledged to restore Israel relations; transition continuing without confirmed complications. Sixth: Venezuela earthquake Day 17 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing. Maduro government continues to restrict USAID and FEMA humanitarian access. De la Espriella's Colombia (T-28 to inauguration) will face immediate cross-border humanitarian pressure upon taking office.

items.summary: Thursday's equity session delivered the most analytically significant market signal of the post-MOU acute stress period: despite confirmed US-Iran military exchanges for a third consecutive day in and around the Strait of Hormuz, US markets closed materially higher across all three major indices. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 139.02 points (+0.3%) to close at 52,478.41. The S&P 500 gained 0.8% to finish at 7,543.64. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.3% (+336.24 points) to 26,206.89, driven by strong performance from AI and semiconductor names. The session's defining catalyst was the SK Hynix IPO: the South Korean chipmaker priced at $149 per share and raised $26.51 billion, the largest-ever market debut by a foreign company on Nasdaq and the largest foreign company IPO in US exchange history by proceeds. The SK Hynix offering was oversubscribed, driven by investor demand for AI infrastructure exposure — specifically, SK Hynix's HBM3E (high-bandwidth memory) products that are integral to Nvidia H100 and H200 GPU production. The fact that the largest-ever foreign company Nasdaq debut occurred in the midst of active US-Iran military exchanges is the market's most definitive statement on the MOU's survival probability. Entering Friday's session, Schwab's morning market update characterizes the setup as 'Strait Attacks Flare but Chips Lead Early Gains' — confirming the AI/semiconductor sector's role as the market's primary narrative override for geopolitical risk. Two economic data releases from Thursday bear watch: first, initial jobless claims for the week ended July 4 came in at 215,000 — 2,000 below the prior week and below the Zacks consensus estimate of 223,000 — signaling continued labor market resilience despite the compound macro pressures of Hormuz re-escalation, Russian fuel crisis, and elevated interest rates. Second, existing home sales for June unexpectedly fell to 4.09 million units (seasonally adjusted annual rate), missing the 4.19 million consensus estimate. The housing sector weakness is consistent with the Warsh Fed's 3.50-3.75% hold at elevated rates — mortgage rates remain prohibitive for new listings. WTI crude entering Friday at approximately $75 per barrel reflects the re-escalation premium that has held since the July 7 oil-sanctions reimposition: this is above the $74 normalization floor established at the June 19 MOU signing, but for the wrong reason — it reflects war-risk premium, not deal-confidence. The oil market is pricing between $73 and $80 as the acute-stress range. Any move below $73 would signal de-escalation confidence returning; any move above $78-80 would signal escalation premium intensifying ahead of a weekend potentially at risk of further exchange.

items.summary: Four secondary economic-legislative threads entering July 10 morning. First: One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) advances to Law Day 11. The Medicaid work requirement and SNAP reduction provisions are in active implementation across 18 states. No federal court has issued a preliminary injunction or stay as of the July 10 morning cycle. The absence of a legal stay entering Day 11 narrows the window for emergency judicial intervention before implementation machinery becomes self-reinforcing. Legal challenges remain active in multiple federal circuits, with the most consequential pending before the D.C. Circuit, but no stay order has issued. Second: DOT BUILD (Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development) grants totaling $1.73 billion were announced by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on July 7 — 127 projects across 52 states, territories, and the District of Columbia. The portfolio includes $1.3 billion for roads and bridges, $169.9 million for transit, $136.8 million for ports (including $8.5 million for Alaska Railroad Corporation for Seward Port dock expansion), and $62 million for truck parking across five states. The scale of eligible applications — nearly 1,200 applications requesting $14.5 billion combined — reflects persistent infrastructure investment demand well above available federal appropriations. Third: Section 122 (broad national-security tariff authority) stands at T-14 days to the July 24 expiry of the current 12.5% tariff schedule on 46 countries. The USTR Section 301 public hearing concluded July 7; the post-hearing review period is now active. The July 24 expiry creates a binary outcome: extension/modification of the existing 12.5% schedule, or lapse with significant trade-flow disruption. Canadian tariff hearings are being held separately this week — 10% tariffs on Canadian goods — creating a parallel bilateral trade track running concurrently with the Section 122 multilateral framework. Fourth: Trump's personal cryptocurrency profits, newly disclosed in scale, are creating a conflict-of-interest complication for the Senate crypto market structure bill that Republican leaders want to bring to the floor in July. The conflict has been cited as a sticking point in negotiations. The crypto bill's July floor target may slip if the conflict disclosure becomes a procedural blocking mechanism for Democratic votes needed for cloture.

items.summary: The Chelan Hills Fire enters Day 6 as the PNW's highest-priority active fire management concern, with the session defined by its first sustained test under Red Flag Warning conditions since achieving 50% containment on Day 5. The fire's official ICS-209 footprint stands at approximately 9,735 acres in Douglas County, east of Lake Chelan — though some reporting has cited estimates above 20,000 acres, a source discrepancy that reflects the difficulty of perimeter assessment in the terrain and smoke conditions of the initial containment phase. At 50% containment entering Day 6, the Chelan Hills Fire has made categorical progress from its Day 3 zero-containment posture (which coincided with 100 or more structures destroyed and the confirmed fatality). The Douglas County Fire Marshal has characterized the structural loss as the worst in the county's 30-year recorded fire history. Day 6 operational posture: with Red Flag Warning conditions active (sustained winds 15-25mph, gusts to 35mph, relative humidity in the critical range), the primary risk is not ignition of new fires but perimeter integrity. A 50% containment line in Red Flag conditions means that 50% of the fire's perimeter remains open and exposed to the exact wind and humidity conditions that historically produce fire behavior capable of reversing containment line work in hours. Personnel are focused on fortifying contained sectors and pre-positioning suppression resources on the uncontained flanks ahead of afternoon peak fire weather. Two secondary fires require monitoring. Luna Fire: ignited in North Cascades National Park west of Ross Lake; approximately 5.5 acres as of July 8 reporting; park environment creates wilderness fire management constraints. Mt. Tom Creek Fire: burning on the west side of Olympic National Park in remote terrain; 68 acres as of July 7 reporting; 0% containment in its most recent ICS-209; remoteness limits direct suppression access. Navarre Coulee Fire (approximately 300 acres, 80% contained, Level 1 evacuations only) is effectively resolved and not a primary active suppression concern. NIFC Preparedness Level 4 continues on Day 12 — the first PL4 designation since 2021, indicating that national fire suppression resources are significantly committed. 37 or more large fires are burning nationally. East Cascades Onset Day 13: the PNW's formally designated high-risk fire onset window is now two weeks into its active period.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering July 10 morning, with Longview CSB as the session's highest-specificity short-fuse risk. First: Longview CSB Day 46, T-1 to the July 11 elevated risk window. The brief series has tracked the 90,000-gallon hazardous material storage tank at the Longview facility for 46 days, with elevated monitoring flags issued during prior heat events (the June 14-16 extreme heat event triggered the first acute vapor pressure risk window). For July 11, the brief has identified a 'three-thread convergence' — a combination of ambient temperature, storage cycle timing, and atmospheric conditions that historically correlates with elevated vapor pressure risk for the specific material stored. T-1 means this convergence materializes tomorrow; July 10 is the final pre-convergence monitoring day. No anomalous readings have been confirmed through July 9 evening, but the T-1 designation warrants elevated situational awareness through the July 10-11 window. Second: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) remains closed. The atmospheric river suppression window that provided favorable conditions for Sourdough Fire firefighting operations closed on the night of July 8. Day 6 Sourdough Fire ICS-209 field assessment is the operative pending indicator for SR-20 reopening timeline — the July 9 evening brief identified this as the key pending data point. Skagit hydroelectric dam power restoration is also pending. SR-20 closure affects access to North Cascades National Park and commercial freight movement through the northern Cascades corridor. Third: NSF Newport Oregon ocean observatory remains dark on Day 12 of its monitoring gap. The monitoring gap opened approximately June 28 and continues through an active fire season, an ongoing heat event, and the East Cascades Onset Day 13 period — the coastal atmospheric anchor for PNW fire-weather modeling is absent during the period of highest analytical demand. Reinstallation timeline has not been confirmed. Fourth: Oregon Coast magnitude 5.5 earthquake at 4:35 AM Monday struck under the Pacific Ocean near the Oregon Coast. No structural damage or tsunami alert was confirmed. A 5.5 at the Oregon offshore zone warrants note in the Cascadia subduction zone monitoring context: while this magnitude is well below Cascadia megathrust range, offshore seismic activity in this area is tracked as part of ongoing subduction zone preparation monitoring. Washington drought emergency continues on Day 36 of the fourth consecutive drought year, with statewide snowpack at 50% of normal and 12 counties under emergency declaration.

items.summary: Four primary domestic threads entering July 10 morning. First: Maine Senate race scramble. Graham Platner — the populist political newcomer whom Democrats had recruited to challenge incumbent Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) — ended his campaign after a woman he previously dated publicly accused him of sexual assault. Maine Democrats have until July 27 to select a replacement candidate. The Platner dropout is a material setback for Democratic 2026 Senate cycle math: Collins was considered a potential vulnerable incumbent in a state that has trended toward moderate Republican candidates, and Platner had polled competitively. A July 27 replacement deadline leaves the new nominee with limited time to build name recognition and fundraising infrastructure before the general election. Collins's reelection odds improved materially following the Platner dropout. Second: White House Domestic Policy Council released a 162-page report over the July 4 weekend accusing the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of American History of 'adopting an ideological framework' and functioning as 'a political instrument to divide, dispirit and discourage our citizens' rather than promoting a 'shared national inheritance to be taught or celebrated.' The report — the most extensive executive-branch cultural institution criticism since the Heritage Foundation's Project 2025 education chapters — establishes a rhetorical predicate for potential institutional restructuring, funding reform, or senior leadership changes at the Smithsonian. Third: The Trump administration is holding hearings this week on 10% tariffs against Canadian goods, creating a bilateral trade track running concurrently with the Section 122 multilateral framework (T-14 days to July 24 expiry). The Canadian tariff track is separate from both Section 122 and the USMCA renegotiation discussions. Fourth: Newly disclosed scale of President Trump's personal cryptocurrency-related profits since taking office has emerged as a conflict-of-interest sticking point in Senate negotiations on a crypto market structure bill that Republican leaders want to bring to the floor in July. The disclosure complicates Democratic cloture support and may push the July floor target into August or later. Acting DNI Day 50 is a procedural milestone: the intelligence community is operating without Senate-confirmed leadership for the 50th consecutive day at maximum concurrent workload (Hormuz MOU verification, Lebanon ceasefire monitoring, nuclear timeline assessment, Pakistan insurgency assessment, Russia fuel-crisis intelligence).

items.summary: Two secondary domestic threads entering July 10 morning. First: Measles high-consequence sub-window advances to Day 2. The sub-window (July 9-12) tracks the exposure event from the June 19 Lumen Field USA vs. Australia match — approximately 70,000-plus attendees at the FIFA World Cup group-stage fixture during the measles cluster identification window for the June 15 Belgium vs. Egypt match. Day 1 of the sub-window (July 9) closed clean: no confirmed mass-event clusters in King County or Snohomish County. Georgetown University's FIFA surveillance platform — integrating wastewater DNA sequencing, emergency department syndromic surveillance, and social media health signals — continues active monitoring. CDC coordination with King County Public Health is active. The sub-window closes July 12; each clean day reduces the probability of a confirmed mass-event cluster from the June 19 match. National measles case count remains at 2,104 (CDC June 18 update, the most recent available entering July 10). A confirmed Lumen Field cluster in the July 9-12 sub-window would represent the first demonstrated FIFA super-spreader measles event in the 2026 World Cup series and would likely end any remaining probability of preserving US measles elimination status ahead of the WHO/PAHO review in November 2026. The full cluster identification window for the June 19 match (incubation Day 8 of 14) closes July 10, with Day 1 through Day 2 of the high-consequence presentation sub-window now clean. Second: CISA digital infrastructure protection clean streak advances to Day 70 — no confirmed significant domestic cyberattack against critical infrastructure since CISA's most recent incident designation, despite the Hormuz arc's historically elevated Iran cyber-threat environment.

items.summary: The Pacific Northwest enters July 10 facing the convergence of a second significant heat event and an active fire environment that has not abated since the Chelan Hills ignition cluster on July 4. A new round of intense heat is forecast to grip the region, pushing temperatures in Seattle and Portland toward record territory — the second heat event of the 2026 summer season after the June 14-16 Extreme Heat Warning that coincided with the FIFA Seattle opener. The timing is structurally concerning: Chelan Hills Fire's Day 6 Red Flag test occurs as the second heat wave builds, creating the possibility of fire-weather reinforcement (wind-driven fire spread) compounding with thermal loading (high ambient temperatures reducing fine fuel moisture to critical levels) simultaneously. For the PNW fire management picture entering Friday: six or more large fires remain active across Washington state; Red Flag Warning conditions (15-25mph sustained winds, gusts to 35mph, low relative humidity) are active in eastern Washington; and the East Cascades Onset designation has been active for 13 days, meaning the region's highest-risk fire terrain is in its formal peak-risk window. Super El Niño development is the long-range structural risk overlay: a KPTV report from July 8 confirmed that a Super El Niño is developing, building on the June 22 brief's 61% general El Niño probability and 1-in-4 Super El Niño probability. A Super El Niño event (the most intense category, rarer than standard El Niño) would compound the fourth consecutive year of Washington drought and 50% snowpack deficit with a warmer, drier projected 2026-2027 winter — eliminating any snowpack recovery pathway and setting up a fifth consecutive drought year. The Oregon Coast magnitude 5.5 earthquake at 4:35 AM Monday (Pacific Ocean offshore) produced no confirmed damage or tsunami warning, but is logged in the Cascadia subduction zone monitoring framework. Offshore seismic events in the Oregon-Washington Pacific zone are systematically tracked as part of state and federal preparedness for a potential Cascadia megathrust event. The 5.5 magnitude is well below the threshold of megathrust concern but consistent with ongoing tectonic activity in the region. PNW Climate Week 2026 opens T-3 days (July 13-19, Seattle/Vancouver/Portland) — the week's programming will occur against a backdrop of active fire season, heat events, and the Super El Niño announcement, providing a high-relevance climate signal context for the policy discussions.

items.summary: Five secondary PNW environmental and local threads entering July 10 morning. First: Chelan Hills Fire Day 6 detail. The fire's containment arc — 0% (Day 3), 20% (Day 4), 50% (Day 5) — represents the most rapid sustained containment progress on a fire of this size in the PNW 2026 season. The Day 6 test under Red Flag Warning conditions will determine whether the containment arc continues or whether the afternoon wind event reverses progress on the uncontained flanks. Douglas County fire management is operating on its own resources, supplemented by mutual aid from adjacent counties and USFS Type 3 overhead teams. The most sensitive perimeter sectors for Day 6 are those on the western and northern flanks, where westerly gap winds are the primary spread mechanism. Chelan Hills is the fire most likely to either reach 65%+ containment (positive resolution) or regress to below-40% containment (negative regression) by the July 10 evening brief window. Second: Longview CSB T-1 detail. The July 11 three-thread convergence window is the primary short-fuse infrastructure monitoring concern for July 10-11. The brief series has tracked this convergence for two days (T-2 on July 9, T-1 on July 10). No anomalous readings were reported in the July 9 evening cycle. Monitoring continues through July 11. Third: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory remains dark on Day 12. The coastal atmospheric monitoring gap is compounding with the incoming second heat wave — PNW fire-weather forecasters are operating without the coastal anchor station precisely as the second significant heat event of the season approaches. Fourth: Weekend events. Two events of note running July 10-12 in the PNW: the Northwest Tune-Up Bike and Music Festival in Bellingham (mass gathering on a smoke-impacted potential day if Chelan Hills or adjacent fires produce easterly smoke transport); and West Seattle Summer Fest July 10-12 (outdoor urban event under potential heat advisory conditions). Fifth: NOAA gray whale monitoring above annual pace: Oregon 21 YTD, Washington 17 YTD. Pacific gray whale washup rates above annual pace are tracked as a Cascadia ecosystem indicator in the brief series. Southern Resident Orca calf (L-pod) has now been documented alive for multiple weeks — continued positive signal for the critically endangered population. BPA grid monitoring is active ahead of the incoming heat event; Day 1 demand surge test will come when the heat wave peaks in western Washington.

analyst_summary: July 10, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 4 — the third consecutive session at this level — with the session's defining analytical signature being the dislocation between the Hormuz military picture and the US equity market's response to it. The most important data point entering Friday morning is not a geopolitical development but a market one: Thursday's equity close of Dow +0.3%, S&P +0.8%, Nasdaq +1.3%, anchored by the SK Hynix $26.51B IPO — the largest-ever foreign company Nasdaq debut — represents the equity market's operational verdict that the MOU's formal survival thread (the Witkoff/Kushner channel, the no-Kharg-strike constraint, the no-SNSC-void-declaration fact pattern) is credible. The market has observed 14 prior escalation-and-pullback sequences in the 133-day Hormuz arc. It is pricing Trump's 'ceasefire over' language as declaratory maximum-pressure posture rather than an operational termination order. The market is likely correct on the probabilistic distribution of outcomes — the formal instruments of MOU termination remain unused — but it may be underpricing the structural deterioration that the July 7 oil-sanctions reimposition represents: removing the Iranian crude export waiver eliminates the MOU's central economic incentive for Iranian compliance, creating a material incentive for Tehran to escalate Hormuz interference intensity in ways that could eventually produce a Kharg interdiction or naval blockade reinstatement. The weekend is the highest-risk window for a Kharg strike or escalation step that re-prices market assumptions. On the domestic infrastructure front, the July 10 session carries two time-specific risks: Longview CSB T-1 to the July 11 three-thread convergence (the most precisely specified short-fuse infrastructure risk in the brief record for this period), and Chelan Hills Fire Day 6 Red Flag test (50% containment entering Red Flag conditions with afternoon wind peak). The Maine Senate Platner dropout and the WH DPC Smithsonian report are the domestic story-line developments, but neither is an acute operational risk in the immediate 24-hour window. Acting DNI Day 50 is a milestone marker: 50 consecutive days of maximum concurrent IC workload without Senate-confirmed leadership represents a structural institutional risk that accretes quietly across the session. Three primary watchitems entering the July 10 session: first, weekend Kharg Island and Hormuz monitoring — the absence of a Kharg strike through Day 3 is the Vibe 4 anchor; any CENTCOM confirmation of Kharg operations or Iran SNSC formal MOU-void declaration drops this to Vibe 3 immediately; second, Chelan Hills Day 6 Red Flag test — afternoon fire weather will determine whether the containment arc continues or reverses; third, Longview CSB July 11 convergence preparation — no anomalous readings through July 9 evening, but T-1 warrants active monitoring through the day.
